canonical_statement: For every smooth real-valued function u on the standard round unit two-sphere, log((1/(4*pi)) integral exp(u)) is at most (1/(4*pi)) integral u plus (1/(16*pi)) times the Dirichlet energy of u.
domain_and_universes: u : SmoothSphereFunction, an ambient C-infinity representative restricted to Metric.sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace Real (Fin 3)) 1; Prop in universe 0
conclusion: Real.log ((1 / (4 * Real.pi)) * integral (Real.exp composed with u)) <= (1 / (4 * Real.pi)) * integral u + (1 / (16 * Real.pi)) * dirichletEnergy u

encoding.area_measure: the two-dimensional Hausdorff measure on the sphere subtype
encoding.smoothness: a global ambient C-infinity extension; this is a concrete sufficient encoding of a smooth sphere function
encoding.gradient: ambient gradient projected orthogonally to the tangent plane
encoding.normalization: area 4*pi form with mean coefficient 1/(4*pi) and sharp energy coefficient 1/(16*pi)

source_crosswalk: The Springer primary-source abstract for DOI 10.1007/BF01212171 explicitly says C-infinity functions on the two-dimensional sphere and gives the constrained positivity form. Algebraically setting eta = u - log((1/(4*pi))*integral exp u), using area 4*pi and invariance of the gradient under constants, gives this normalized logarithmic form. Full article-page and errata review remains an H-gate task, not a statement-elaboration prerequisite.
